exposure: Maternal age (advanced maternal age ≥ 35 years vs. young pregnant women)
outcome: Labour progression times (cervical dilation to 10 cm, fetal station to 2 cm)
cohort: The study retrospectively analyzed 1573 nulliparous women delivering at Kinan Hospital in Japan, with the primary comparison focusing on labour progression between those of advanced maternal age and young women who achieved spontaneous vaginal delivery.
finding: The study found no clear impact of maternal age on labour progression among nulliparous women who had spontaneous vaginal delivery, after excluding those who underwent emergency caesarean section or received intravenous uterotonic agents.
mod_finding: Women of advanced maternal age had higher percentages of emergency caesarean sections and intravenous uterotonic agent administration, and differences in vacuum delivery status were detected compared to young women.
